content.thinking:
I'll plan out the treant's full design in one careful pass rather than testing incrementally—sizing it around 4.5 meters to tower appropriately, with a wide stance, outstretched branch-like arms, an antlered crown of yellow leaves, a bearded bark face, a glowing green chest crack, and details like mushrooms and ivy. I'm setting up the coordinate conventions (facing +Z, left as +X) before building out the joint structure.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a hip root joint, a spine chain running up through several points to the chest, then a neck chain of two spans leading to a head joint, with the head carrying a role and the jaw parented off it. I'm working through naming conventions for each chain so the joints and spans line up correctly between hips, spine, neck, and head.

Moving to arms, I'm placing shoulders symmetrically on either side and defining a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain with slight downward droop for a natural T-pose, making sure the naming scheme correctly produces a tip joint at the wrist so fingers and thumb chains can parent off it.

For the hands, I'm setting up five two-span digit chains per side, giving around 10 chains and 30 joints total for fingers, then moving to legs with hip-knee-ankle chains spaced for a wide stance, keeping the overall joint budget around 160.

For the torso mesh, I'm planning to loft/sweep along the spine chain from hips to chest, using a radius function that varies by t to create a natural taper—narrower at the waist, wider at the chest with an elliptical cross-section.

Now for materials: I'm designing the bark paint using grain and mottle noise functions, with colors ranging from dark brown to light tan for the base bark, plus a moss overlay in greens applied where the surface normal points upward, blending them via a composed paint function.

Darkening the undersides where normals face downward for a simple shading effect. For roots, I'll add five flat sweeping shapes per foot spreading outward along the ground.

Modeling each root as a tapering tube curving from the ankle down into the floor, with radius shrinking from 0.2 near the bone to 0.05 at the tip, keeping the path close to the ground so it visually plants into the surface.

Now I'm shaping the main foot mass as a flattened lofted sweep anchored at the ankle, widening outward and downward to form a flattened pad that rests at the floor, then setting up the leg as a chained sweep with a tapering radius profile.

Thinking through the hip-to-ankle radius tapering, I'm wrapping the hip bone chain and tying the spine chain back to the hips as its root joint, with the pelvis represented by a scaled sphere part at the hip position. Then I'm sizing the leg radius to slightly overlap the pelvis for a seamless joint, and defining the arm chain with tapering radii from shoulder to elbow to wrist, giving the forearm extra thickness.

Now I'm adding big shoulder pad masses as scaled spheres with mossy bark texture, then building the hand with a palm sphere and five long tapering fingers radiating outward with slight curling and fanning offsets based on wrist position.

Still defining finger geometry...

Now I'm designing the head: a skull sphere with a brow ridge, cone nose, glowing amber eyes under the brow, and a lichen-grey beard built from tapering spike shapes swept around the chin, plus a separate jaw part attached below the head joint.

Next I'm building the antler crown, sweeping curved catmull-spline branches outward from the top of the head with symmetric left/right pairs, then adding smaller sub-branches that sprout off points along each main branch.

I'm scattering leaf-textured cards along the antler tips and branches using facing frames, then adding a similar ivy leaf scatter across the torso surface for extra organic detail.

Still working out the vine sweep orientation...

I think I'll just use drape instead -- draping a catmull path over the torso surface for ivy vines and moss sweeps, with a thin radius and vine color. For the glowing chest crack I'll drape a zigzag line on the front with a glow-green sweep, and consider adding a torus-ring knot detail near the chest.

For mushrooms, I'm planning a helper that sticks a cylinder stem plus a hemisphere cap onto scattered leg hits, colored in orange-brown, filtered by normal direction so they sit naturally on the leg surfaces.

I'm also adding bark texture via flattened box shards scattered across the torso with painted bark coloring, plus some subtle knot spheres on the limbs, kept moderate so it doesn't get too busy. For the heavy Warcraft-style shoulders, I'm planning branch-stub spurs — three small spikes per shoulder with leaf cards attached.

Now I'm sketching elbow thorns as rigid spikes on the elbow bone, and a canopy of branches with leaves sweeping up from the upper back. For torso attachment points, I'm settling on an explicit spine chain with three named joints (no extra tip), so the chest attachment uses the third spine joint directly rather than relying on nearest-joint placement, avoiding confusion with the pelvis/hip root joint.

Spine chains parent to the hips, while neck and arms parent to the chest joint, and legs parent to the hips. For arm chains with three names, the wrist is just the last joint in the array, so I'll index it directly rather than relying on a separate tip property, and shoulder pads attach to the first arm joint. I also need to make sure the torso surface API accepts sweeps properly, and that scattering leaves on legs works with nested sweep arrays passed to the surface call.

Now I'm designing the leaf textures as SVGs -- an ivy leaf (green, lobed) and a maple leaf (yellow, five-lobed), each with a simple vein path, sized for card rendering. I'm also planning moss tuft cards with blade shapes scattered on upward-facing surfaces, and considering a lichen strand texture hanging from the chin, positioned using the jaw's facing points.

Working out the skull geometry now: placing the skull sphere center and scaling for the face front and chin regions, adding a lower jaw piece near the jaw joint, and defining beard spikes hanging down from the jaw with varying lengths and a tapering sweep, tinted in a pale lichen color.

Now I'm placing the eye sockets as dark spheres with glowing amber eyes slightly forward, plus brow ridges built from capsule shapes angled across the forehead.

Still shaping facial features...

Now I'm attaching the antler crown to the head joint and plotting back canopy branches that sweep up and outward from the chest, with leaf clusters forming at the branch tips.

For each leaf cluster I'm generating randomized frames biased upward and outward, then batching the resulting leaf cards per bone and texture so the crown, chest, and arm clusters each collect their own frame arrays before rendering.

Simplifying to a spike helper for branches with leaf frames at the tips, then checking overall height proportions—treant body plus antlers should reach about 5.9m so it still towers over a human, with head top around 5.15m. Now I'm working out leg hip placement starting around 2.0m.

For the toes, I'm fanning five root shapes around each foot in an arc from -70 to 70 degrees plus two back roots, tapering each from a wide ankle-joint base down to a thin tip near ground level so they splay naturally without poking below the floor. I'm reconsidering whether to skip the foot loft entirely and just use a simpler shape instead.

I decide to loft the foot from three stations near the ankle, arch, and toe area, sized so each sits flush at ground level, accepting minor rounding dips as negligible. For the leg, I set ankle, knee, and hip joint positions with tapering tube radii, skipping separate toe joints since the roots are rigid off the ankle.

I build the leg as a three-point chain (hip, knee, ankle) with a smooth tapering radius array, do the same for the arm with its own radius profile, and add a scaled palm sphere near the wrist for the hand. For the torso I define a spine chain curving from the hips up through the chest, with its own paired radius falloff.

I'm writing a small lerp helper to interpolate waist and chest radii, add shoulder mass as scaled spheres textured with bark and moss, and build the neck as a tapered sweep chain feeding into the head, rooting everything at the hips.

Now I'm checking that arm shoulder joints sit properly inset within the torso radius, then drafting glowing eye parts and chest crack geometry as draped surface paths across the torso and lungs for a worn, fractured look.

I'm now adding vine growth along the shoulder using diagonal drape paths, with leaf cards distributed along each vine via sampled points.

Rather than letting the leaves face the path tangent, I'm projecting each sample point onto the torso surface to get proper normals, then orienting the ivy cards to lean outward and flow downward along the body.

Designing leaf shapes now...

Now I'm setting ivy colors with green fill, lighter vein stroke, and a darker outline, then sketching the moss tuft blades and bark plate geometry scattered across the torso and limbs for texture.

For mushrooms, I'm scattering clusters near the legs with small stick stems and rounded orange caps, positioning each cap just above its stem, and checking that the scatter filter correctly passes hit data through.

Now I'm setting up the module exports with metadata and the build function signature, then importing the core builder utilities, math helpers, path curves, paint functions, texture, and glow kit needed for the asset.

For the bark material, I'm layering grain-based base color, mottled moss patches on upward-facing normals, cell-based cracks where Voronoi distances converge, and darker tones on downward normals, with noise breaking up the highlights and base texture.

Now I'm building the treant skeleton, starting with hips and a spine chain following a curved spline through three joints, then branching into a neck chain and head joint off the chest.

Placing the jaw sphere so the face front extends slightly forward, and deciding to skip adding a separate mouth line or teeth since the beard will cover that area.

Now I'm setting up the torso structure: sweeping the spine chain for the body with a bark color, adding a pelvis part using a scaled sphere at the hips bone, sweeping the neck with a linear radius, and looping through left/right sides to build the arms.

For each side I'm defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints as a chain parented to the chest, sweeping the arm geometry with varying radii, then setting up the wrist joint to attach a palm part and fingers afterward.

Now I'm adding an elbow spike detail positioned slightly off the elbow joint, and a shoulder pad sphere scaled and positioned near the top of the arm, both bound to the arm's joints for proper movement.

Then I'm sketching out spurs on the shoulder pad, mirroring the leg structure, and setting up the frame collection system with leaf arrays and end cards. For the crown, I'm defining a swept path through several control points that curves up and back from the skull, using a tapered tube shape anchored into the skull geometry.

For the finer details, I'm adding sub-branches along the main crown sweep with alternating directions and leaf clusters at tips, plus considering small leaf sprigs at fingertips attached via wrist-based frame arrays per arm.

Now I'm writing a helper function that scatters leaf frames in a small radial burst around a point, using random angles and heights...

Setting up the beard geometry, computing tapered strand lengths and curved paths along the chin.

Scattering moss tufts on top surfaces where normals point upward, then collecting all torso, arm, and leg sweeps into surface groups to place ivy leaf cards across the body with varied lean, bend, and spin parameters.

Switching to stacked cylinder rings instead since the torus faces the wrong axis, building a dark outer ring, a lighter inner ring, and a glowing green cylinder for the chest knot using moved hit frames.

Verifying the chain sweep's radius keys and confirming the leg position stays unchanged, then writing the file.
